To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain can influence the immune system, and the immune can influence the brain.

(a) the brain and the immune system interact; (b) the immune system can be modulated by the brain through the autonomic nervous system and by the endocrine system; (c) the brain can influence immune system function through the central nervous system; (d) the immune system is capable of producing neuroactive compounds; and (e) immune system function can influence behavior.

the role of psychological factors in health and disease, the mechanisms underlying these phenomena, and the development of new treatments based on this understanding.
understanding the role that brain and behavior play in shaping the immune system, and the implications of this knowledge for understanding human health and disease.

psychoneuroimmunity research has demonstrated that the brain and the immune system interact, and that these interactions can have profound implications for health and disease.

psychoneuroimmuno-logical research has established the existence of bi-directional communication between the central nervous system and the immune system and that this communication has important implications for health and disease.
the immune system is not a separate entity but an integrated part of the whole organism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune system can be modulated by the central nervous system and by behavior, and that this modulation has implications for health and disease.

the immune system is a complex system that interacts with other systems in the body and the environment in a multitude of ways, and that these interactions are influenced by psychological factors, including stress, emotions, and social relationships.
the immune system is a dynamic, complex, and adaptive network of cells and organs that is influenced by a wide range of factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system is a complex, dynamic system with multiple levels of organization.
the brain and the immune system are intimately connected and that this relationship is bidirectional and dynamic.
the immune system is not autonomous but rather a part of the brain and body, which is regulated by the brain and body.
